review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: Implant an optic fiber over region P to target the somata of the P-to-Q projecting neurons.
errors.issue: This tests the Q-projecting cell population, including possible collateral outputs. Projection targeting does not isolate P-to-Q transmission; the answer repeatedly claims pathway necessity without this limitation.

errors.quote: Targeting inhibitory opsin expression exclusively to P neurons that project to Q (O2) isolates the specific anatomical pathway.
errors.issue: O2 gives access to neurons defined by one target, not proof that those neurons lack other targets. O1 itself also does not establish single-neuron collateralization; it must be tested or bounded.

errors.quote: start at a theoretical safe maximum (e.g., 10 mW) and reduce until behavioral or physiological effects titrate
errors.issue: An unspecified maximum is not a demonstrated safe or effective setting. A behavioral deficit cannot validate neural suppression; require independent physiology, timing/recovery and preparation-specific optical/thermal validation.

errors.quote: and locomotor metrics remain unchanged, you can conclude the P-to-Q projection is specifically necessary for cue retrieval.
errors.issue: Motor measurements and reporter controls do not exclude inhibition-induced cue perception, attention or preparation deficits. There is no task-matched sensory probe, movement-free recovery gap or timing-control intervention.

errors.quote: Percentage of correct choices on light-ON versus light-OFF trials.
errors.issue: The denominator, omissions/aborts, animal-level sample-size plan and precision/equivalence criteria are missing. These omissions materially limit both positive and negative interpretation.

errors.quote: the optical shielding is insufficient, and the visible light is acting as a distracter.
errors.issue: A control-group deficit can also arise from heating, sound or other procedural effects. The observation identifies a nonspecific light-associated effect, not its unique sensory mechanism.

rationale: Clear basic group-by-light design and animal-level mixed model, but the intervention does not answer the projection-specific question as claimed. Functional validation and the sensory/motor discrimination need substantial redesign; brevity itself is not penalized.
reference_guardrails: O1 establishes that population P has two targets, not that every Q-projecting neuron collateralizes. Do not assume either overlap or disjointness; validate or retain the limitation.

Projection-defined somatic inhibition tests a population and all its affected outputs. Local Q-terminal intervention is preferable for a pathway claim but also needs actual transmission and off-target validation.
Suppression in neuronal somata does not guarantee suppression of terminal transmission. Validate physiological onset, sustained effect, offset recovery and rebound at the actual behavioral settings.

Reduced normal performance supports a conditional causal requirement, not memory storage or an exclusive retrieval computation. Cue perception, attention, maintenance and motor preparation remain alternatives.
Light offset is not necessarily inhibition offset. A choice made after light ends can correctly report an earlier retrieval deficit; outcome timing alone is not a rebound diagnosis.
Movement adjustment/matching after intervention and conditioning on response completion can bias inference. Report all randomized trials and use experimental motor/sensory dissociations.
A nonsignificant control effect is not equivalence. Predefine biologically meaningful bounds and obtain enough precision to exclude consequential confounds.
Two pathways or epochs can both be necessary. Effects in an other-projection control do not by themselves invalidate the tested pathway contribution.

Numbers missing from the packet may be proposed as pilot settings; no specific opsin, surgical coordinate or animal count is mandatory. Operational calibration and justified independent-animal sampling are required.

Reference correction: population-level divergence must not be described as demonstrated single-neuron collateralization. Terminal effects on intended local Q signaling are part of the intervention, not automatically an off-target artifact.

review_sources.title: Mahn et al. (2016): biophysical constraints of presynaptic optogenetic inhibition
review_sources.scope: Reviewer-only primary-source check of terminal efficacy, paradoxical release and offset rebound; no particular construct is required by the question.

review_sources.title: Montgomery, Nyhan and Torres: post-treatment conditioning
review_sources.scope: Authors summarize their methodological paper on adjustment/selection after treatment. Used only by reviewer, not candidates.
